blocks.raw: # Payment rules
blocks.text: Payment rules

blocks.raw: After you have set up your accounts and are able to send and receive payments, you can start automating your payment flows. For example, when a payment is received into an account, you might want to automatically forward 10% of the money to to an external company account and the remaining 90% to an external client account. This can be done using our Payment Rule functionality.
blocks.text: After you have set up your accounts and are able to send and receive payments, you can start automating your payment flows. For example, when a payment is received into an account, you might want to automatically forward 10% of the money to to an external company account and the remaining 90% to an external client account. This can be done using our Payment Rule functionality.

blocks.raw: Before creating any rules, you will need to have Accounts and Beneficiaries setup, as rules need a Modulr account to be applied to, and at least one beneficiary's unique reference as a destination.
blocks.text: Before creating any rules, you will need to have Accounts and Beneficiaries setup, as rules need a Modulr account to be applied to, and at least one beneficiary's unique reference as a destination.

blocks.raw: ## Types of rules
blocks.text: Types of rules

blocks.raw: ### Split
blocks.text: Split

blocks.raw: Incoming payments are automatically split into specified percentages to beneficiaries. Split percentages can be specified up to 2 decimal places.
blocks.text: Incoming payments are automatically split into specified percentages to beneficiaries. Split percentages can be specified up to 2 decimal places.

blocks.raw: ### Conditional Split
blocks.text: Conditional Split

blocks.raw: Incoming payments are automatically split into specified percentages to beneficiaries until a fixed amount is met. Thereafter, incoming payments can be automatically split to a different set of beneficiaries, or can remain in the account.
blocks.text: Incoming payments are automatically split into specified percentages to beneficiaries until a fixed amount is met. Thereafter, incoming payments can be automatically split to a different set of beneficiaries, or can remain in the account.

blocks.raw: ### Sweep
blocks.text: Sweep

blocks.raw: At a specified frequency, all money in an account will be automatically transferred into a beneficiary account. This process runs at 3pm UK time. Optional settings allow the rule to only run if the balance is above a certain amount, and to leave a certain amount in the account after the sweep has run.
blocks.text: At a specified frequency, all money in an account will be automatically transferred into a beneficiary account. This process runs at 3pm UK time. Optional settings allow the rule to only run if the balance is above a certain amount, and to leave a certain amount in the account after the sweep has run.

blocks.raw: ### Funding
blocks.text: Funding

blocks.raw: When there is an outgoing payment from an account that does not have sufficient funds, the account can be automatically funded from a secondary account. This rule is only available if the ‘Hold For Funds’ feature has been enabled.
blocks.text: When there is an outgoing payment from an account that does not have sufficient funds, the account can be automatically funded from a secondary account. This rule is only available if the ‘Hold For Funds’ feature has been enabled.

blocks.raw: ## Examples of payment rules
blocks.text: Examples of payment rules

blocks.raw:
**Split**\
Move 7.25% of each incoming payment to a beneficiary.
blocks.text: SplitMove 7.25% of each incoming payment to a beneficiary.

blocks.raw:
**Conditional Split**\
When an incoming payment is received, transfer 10% to B1000001 and 5% to B1000002 until 100 GBP has been sent to B1000001. The remaining 85% remains in account. Once the amount of 100 GBP has been met, 100% of incoming payments will be transferred to B1000003.
blocks.text: Conditional SplitWhen an incoming payment is received, transfer 10% to B1000001 and 5% to B1000002 until 100 GBP has been sent to B1000001. The remaining 85% remains in account. Once the amount of 100 GBP has been met, 100% of incoming payments will be transferred to B1000003.

blocks.raw:
**Sweep**\
Each day all funds will be automatically transferred to B1000001.
blocks.text: SweepEach day all funds will be automatically transferred to B1000001.

blocks.raw:
```text
{
    "name": "Sweep Example",
    "type": "SWEEP",
    "accountId": "A1000001",
    "data": {
        "daysToRun": [
            "MONDAY",
            "TUESDAY",
            "WEDNESDAY",
            "THURSDAY",
            "FRIDAY",
            "SATURDAY",
            "SUNDAY"
        ],
        "frequency": "Daily",
        "destinationId": "B1000001"
    }
}
```

**Funding**\
The account A1000001 will be funded from secondary account A1000002 if required.
blocks.text: FundingThe account A1000001 will be funded from secondary account A1000002 if required.

blocks.raw: **Example Scenario**
blocks.text: Example Scenario

blocks.raw: *Collecting 10% commission automatically from each Modulr Customer account into one Modulr account, which then gets transferred daily to an external account.*
blocks.text: Collecting 10% commission automatically from each Modulr Customer account into one Modulr account, which then gets transferred daily to an external account.

blocks.raw: To do this you will need to set up a Split rule on all your Customer accounts that transfers 10% of any payment into their accounts into your main Modulr account, then setup a daily Sweep rule on your main Modulr account.
